payload.task_text:
I am preparing for a faculty meeting where we need to review quiz performance across our Fall 2014 courses. I need you to pull quiz data from our learning management system for all courses offered in that semester and summarize the results.

Scope definition (important, follow exactly): our LMS hosts the same subjects across multiple semesters (Fall 2013, Spring 2013, Spring 2014, Fall 2014), and the semester is identified by the suffix in the course name. "Fall 2014 courses" means exactly the courses whose Canvas course name ends with "(Fall 2014)": Applied Analytics & Algorithms (Fall 2014), Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2014), Creative Computing & Culture (Fall 2014), Data-Driven Design (Fall 2014), Environmental Economics & Ethics (Fall 2014), Foundations of Finance (Fall 2014), and Global Governance & Geopolitics (Fall 2014). Do not include any course whose name ends with a different semester suffix, and do not select courses by date ranges or enrollment terms — match on the course-name suffix only. Among these seven courses, only the ones that actually have quizzes in the LMS should appear in the outputs (a course with no quizzes at all is omitted entirely).

For each of those Fall 2014 courses, gather the quiz titles, the number of student submissions per quiz, the average score, the minimum score, and the maximum score. Count every quiz submission recorded in Canvas for that quiz regardless of its submission date, and compute the average/minimum/maximum over the submission scores. Then create an Excel spreadsheet called Quiz_Performance.xlsx in the workspace. The spreadsheet should have a sheet named "Quiz Details" with columns Course, Quiz_Title, Submissions, Avg_Score, Min_Score, and Max_Score. The Course column must contain the full Canvas course name including the "(Fall 2014)" suffix, e.g. "Creative Computing & Culture (Fall 2014)". The Avg_Score, Min_Score, and Max_Score should be rounded to two decimal places. Sort the rows first by Course name alphabetically, then by Quiz_Title alphabetically within each course.

Also add a second sheet called "Course Summary" that aggregates at the course level over the same quiz-bearing Fall 2014 courses. It should have columns Course (again the full course name with the "(Fall 2014)" suffix), Total_Quizzes (number of quizzes in that course), Total_Submissions (sum across all quizzes), and Overall_Avg_Score which is the weighted average of quiz scores across all submissions for that course rounded to two decimal places, i.e. sum(avg_score * submissions) / sum(submissions) over the course's quizzes. Sort alphabetically by Course.

Finally, create a PowerPoint presentation called Quiz_Report.pptx in the workspace. The first slide should be a title slide with the title "Fall 2014 Quiz Performance Report" and subtitle "Faculty Meeting Summary". Then create one dedicated slide per quiz-bearing Fall 2014 course with the course name as the title and a text body listing the number of quizzes, total submissions, and overall average score for that course. Add a final slide with the title "Key Takeaways" and body text stating which course had the highest overall average score and which had the lowest.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, keep the large quiz-submission reads outside the main context with exactly one parallel collector wave, freeze the gathered statistics into a single JSON handoff file, and let the main agent itself build both deliverables — no planning sub-agent, no second wave.

The main agent first resolves the runtime workspace, calls canvas_list_courses(include_ended=true) once, and retains exactly the seven fixed Fall 2014 courses by full-name suffix "(Fall 2014)" (never by date range or enrollment term). Then, natively in parallel, it calls canvas_list_quizzes once per retained course and records each course's literal quiz_ids. A course with zero quizzes is omitted from all outputs. Before dispatch, freeze one assignment manifest entry per quiz-bearing course: course_id|course_name|quiz_ids.

Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 3 explore sub-agents in parallel, one per quiz-bearing Fall 2014 course below. Omit zero-quiz courses from this wave.

   1. explore 0 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): Collector for course_id=7 "Creative Computing & Culture (Fall 2014)": fetch the full quiz-submission records for every quiz in its course (canvas quiz-submission listing, per_page=100, follow pagination.has_page/pagination.has_more, and always read the FULL JSON from the output_path file when the chat preview is truncated); count every recorded submission regardless of date; compute per quiz Submissions (count), Avg_Score, Min_Score, Max_Score over the submission scores; aggregate at course level Total_Quizzes, Total_Submissions, and Overall_Avg_Score = sum(avg_score * submissions) / sum(submissions); and return ONLY the compact JSON {course_id, course_name, quizzes: [{quiz_title, submissions, avg_score, min_score, max_score}], total_quizzes, total_submissions, overall_avg_score}. Strictly read-only with respect to Canvas; do not write workspace files, do not return the raw row set.
   2. explore 1 (enterprise-data-analyst 1): Collector for course_id=17 "Foundations of Finance (Fall 2014)" — same literal recipe, only its assignment string substituted.
   3. explore 2 (enterprise-data-analyst 2): Collector for course_id=21 "Global Governance & Geopolitics (Fall 2014)" — same literal recipe, only its assignment string substituted.

After Wave 1, the main agent verifies every handoff in one single pass (exactly one per manifest entry, non-null statistics, submission counts > 0), then freezes ALL rows into workspace/quiz_data.json — the single handoff for the outputs — and builds both deliverables itself with no further delegation: (a) Quiz_Performance.xlsx with sheet "Quiz Details" (Course, Quiz_Title, Submissions, Avg_Score, Min_Score, Max_Score; full course names including the "(Fall 2014)" suffix; scores rounded to two decimals; sorted by Course then Quiz_Title) and sheet "Course Summary" (Course, Total_Quizzes, Total_Submissions, Overall_Avg_Score; sorted by Course), reading both populated ranges back; (b) Quiz_Report.pptx with a title slide "Fall 2014 Quiz Performance Report" / subtitle "Faculty Meeting Summary", one slide per quiz-bearing course titled with the full course name and listing its quiz count, total submissions and overall average score, and a final "Key Takeaways" slide naming the courses with the highest and lowest overall average scores, verified through presentation info and text extraction. Finally run ONE reconciliation turn covering the workbook read-back and the deck, then call claim_done. Do not dispatch any agent after Wave 1, do not add a verification wave, and do not expose raw submission rows to the main context.

nodes.text:
You are collecting quiz performance data from a Canvas LMS for a faculty report. You have read-only Canvas tools. Do not modify anything in Canvas.

SCOPE (follow exactly): The LMS hosts the same subjects across multiple semesters (Fall 2013, Spring 2013, Spring 2014, Fall 2014); the semester is encoded in the course name suffix. "Fall 2014 courses" = courses whose Canvas course name ends EXACTLY with "(Fall 2014)". The seven expected courses are:
- Applied Analytics & Algorithms (Fall 2014)
- Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2014)
- Creative Computing & Culture (Fall 2014)
- Data-Driven Design (Fall 2014)
- Environmental Economics & Ethics (Fall 2014)
- Foundations of Finance (Fall 2014)
- Global Governance & Geopolitics (Fall 2014)
Select strictly by the name suffix — do NOT filter by dates, start/end, or enrollment term. Exclude every course with any other suffix.

STEPS:
1. List all accessible courses: canvas_list_courses with include_ended=true (Fall 2014 courses may be concluded/ended). If any of the seven expected names are not present, cross-check via canvas_list_account_courses(account_id=1, completed=true), and/or canvas_list_account_courses(account_id=1) without filters. Record course_id and the EXACT full course name for each of the seven Fall 2014 courses. Report any expected course that cannot be found.
2. For each Fall 2014 course: canvas_list_quizzes(course_id) to enumerate ALL quizzes (id and exact title). A course with zero quizzes is excluded from all detail reporting — list it separately.
3. For each quiz: canvas_list_quiz_submissions(course_id, quiz_id). Count EVERY submission record returned, regardless of submission date, attempt number, or workflow state. Collect the 'score' field of each submission. Watch for submissions with null/missing score.
4. For each quiz compute WITHOUT any rounding:
   - submissions = total number of submission records
   - scored_count = number of submissions with a non-null score
   - score_sum = sum of the non-null scores
   - min_score = minimum non-null score
   - max_score = maximum non-null score
   If a quiz has zero submissions, set score_sum/min_score/max_score to null and flag it.

DELIVERABLE: Your final message must contain exactly one JSON block in this shape (plain numbers, no rounding, exact strings as Canvas returns them), followed by at most two sentences noting anomalies:
{
  "fall2014_courses": [
    {
      "course": "<exact Canvas course name>",
      "course_id": <number>,
      "quizzes": [
        {"quiz_id": <number>, "quiz_title": "<exact title>", "submissions": <int>, "scored_count": <int>, "score_sum": <number>, "min_score": <number>, "max_score": <number>}
      ]
    }
  ],
  "courses_without_quizzes": ["<exact course name>"],
  "missing_expected_courses": ["<expected name>"],
  "null_score_submissions": <int total across all quizzes>,
  "anomalies": "<short text or 'none'>"
}
Include in fall2014_courses only courses that have at least one quiz; put quiz-less Fall 2014 courses in courses_without_quizzes.
Collect Canvas Fall 2014 quiz data

Follow-up on your Fall 2014 quiz data collection. Problem: your min_score/max_score values came from sampling/inference ("sampled pages", "inferred from sibling quizzes"). That is not acceptable — we need EXACT values for every quiz, and exact counts verified.

Known context from your prior work: 3 quiz-bearing courses (ids 7, 17, 21), 17 quizzes total, each quiz linked to an assignment_id. You reported per-quiz submissions/scored_count/score_sum as server aggregates.

Tasks (be rigorous, no sampling, no inference):

1. Probe the summary capability: call canvas_list_assignment_submissions(course_id, assignment_id) with per_page=100, page=1 for ONE quiz (e.g., course 21, assignment 197). Report the response shape precisely: does it include a summary/totals block that covers the entire assignment (fields like count, sum, average, min, max, graded_count, submitted_count)? Quote the summary block verbatim. Also note pagination.has_more semantics.

2. If the summary block provides exact min and max of scores plus count and sum: call the same endpoint (page=1 only is fine) for ALL 17 quizzes and extract exact submissions count, score sum, min_score, max_score for each. Cross-check count and sum against your earlier per-quiz numbers; flag ANY discrepancy explicitly.

3. If the summary does NOT provide exact min/max: fully paginate every quiz's assignment (per_page=100, page=1.. until has_more=false) and compute exact count, score_sum, min, max over all records' 'score' fields. Flag any null scores.

4. Attempt multiplicity check: look at submission records — do they carry an 'attempt' field (or similar) indicating attempt number? If any record has attempt > 1, report per-quiz how many such records exist. This tells us whether Canvas quiz-submission records (per attempt) could outnumber assignment-submission records (per student).

5. Re-run canvas_list_quizzes for courses 7, 17, 21 and restate the EXACT quiz titles (verbatim, character-for-character) so we can rule out transcription drift. Also re-confirm the four excluded courses (Applied Analytics & Algorithms, Biochemistry & Bioinformatics, Data-Driven Design, Environmental Economics & Ethics — all "(Fall 2014)") truly have zero quizzes by running canvas_list_quizzes on each of their course ids.

DELIVERABLE: one final JSON block, same structure as before, with exact numbers only:
{
  "fall2014_courses": [{"course_id": n, "course_name": "<exact>", "quizzes": [{"quiz_id": n, "assignment_id": n, "quiz_title": "<exact>", "submissions": n, "scored_count": n, "score_sum": x, "min_score": y, "max_score": z}], "total_submissions": n, "total_score_sum": x}],
  "courses_without_quizzes_verified": true|false,
  "records_with_attempt_gt_1": <int total or per-quiz>,
  "discrepancies_vs_prior_report": "<text or 'none'>"
}
Then a short paragraph quoting the summary-block structure you found.
Verify exact quiz min/max stats

You are verifying the EXACT per-submission score minimum and maximum for ONE Canvas quiz. Read-only task; do not modify anything.

Target: course_id=7, assignment_id=65, quiz_title=CMA 24295, expected_total=1917

Background: Each quiz is linked to a Canvas assignment. The endpoint canvas_list_assignment_submissions(course_id, assignment_id, per_page, page) returns paginated submission records (each with a 'score' field, e.g. "90.00") plus a 'summary' block with the exact 'total_count' and a high-precision 'avg_score'. Pagination info: 'pagination' with page, per_page, total_pages, has_more. One record per student, one attempt each.

Procedure:
1. Call canvas_list_assignment_submissions with course_id and assignment_id from the target, per_page=100, page=1. Record summary.total_count, summary.avg_score, and pagination.total_pages. Check total_count equals the expected_total in your target string; report any mismatch.
2. Walk through EVERY page: page=1,2,...,total_pages (per_page=100). For each page, examine every submission record's 'score'. Maintain a running minimum and running maximum (scores are numeric strings; compare as numbers). Also tally how many records you saw in total and how many have null/missing score (expected 0).
   - If any tool response is truncated/saved to a file by the harness, read that file with your filesystem read tools (in chunks if needed) so no record is skipped.
3. Verify records_seen_sum == total_count. If not, re-fetch missing pages until complete.
4. Sanity check: your min must be <= avg_score <= max.

Deliverable — your final message must be exactly one JSON line in this format (numbers plain, min/max EXACT):
{"course_id": <n>, "assignment_id": <n>, "quiz_title": "<title>", "total_count": <n>, "expected_total": <n>, "records_seen": <n>, "pages_read": <n>, "min_score": <number>, "max_score": <number>, "null_scores": <int>, "avg_score_meta": "<avg from summary>", "notes": "<anomalies or 'none'>"}
The min_score and max_score fields are the critical output — they must be the true minimum/maximum over ALL submission records for this assignment, with every page actually inspected.
Exact per-quiz min/max enumeration

You are verifying the EXACT per-submission score minimum and maximum for ONE Canvas quiz. Read-only task; do not modify anything.
